Chunk 5 'Hold the worry beside the artefact': 'the un-packaged send-off' / 'the artefact' (session-artifact carve-out, repeated use of the same already-established referent); 'did it touch the migration, did the tests really cover the edge' reads as an illustrative example-shape of a worry, not a claim about one specific named migration anywhere in the corpus — understandable as a stand-in. Chunk 6 'Set up the worktree': 'what you built in Module 1 and Module 3' — arc-earned module names (rule 1's own exemption list); 'the two copies' resolves same-sentence (worktree fork just described); 'the two closing lectures' is a same-chunk forward reference to the two lecture links immediately following in this same slide (What packaging is / The gate is a claim too) — not a cross-slide forward pointer, the reader sees blockquote + links on one projected slide. Chunk 7 'Key Concepts': maps to the theory slides mid-deck in the included lecture (chunk 6's 'What packaging is'), per the maintainer block's explicit note that the four lines were chosen so 'the reminders-only test passes by construction' — deliberate in-file forward planting inside an earlier chunk, resolved. Chunk 8 (active, 'Bring to Module 6'): 'the re-send' resolves to this module's own exercise named in chunk 6 ('[Exercise: Diagnose and re-send]'). Chunk 10 'Next': 'Your verifier' and 'one of three eval shapes' resolve to What You'll Learn's own three-shape LO (chunk 3, line 16). Light-touch check of the inactive chunk 8-alt ('Back to the map, one last time', live only in the Northwind four-sitting cut): 'The map' and 'THE TEAM' / 'a move counts when it crosses the wall' are verified arc-earned spine vocabulary — grep confirms 'the map', 'the wall' and the identical soil-line quote are established in lectures/the-whole-map.md and lectures/the-map-filled-in.md, both included by other AE101 module files (plan-mode-done-right.md includes the-whole-map.md; spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md includes the-map-filled-in.md), matching rule 1's own named example ('the map'). No never-named or vague-with-full-history referent found in either branch.

Every cross-file reference names the source by title or claim, not by position: '[Lecture: Reading the return]', '[Lecture: Learning through contrast]', '[Exercise: Fork the worktree, carry the evidence]', '[Exercise: Diagnose and re-send]', '[Lecture: What packaging is]', '[Lecture: The gate is a claim too]' (structural include-links, exempt per rule 13), plus the two Prework supplementary links and four external practitioner links (Entis, Klaassen x2, da Costa), all named by title/author. 'The M1 countermove' (chunk 4) names the source module by its stable architectural number (not a position-dependent locator like 'the opening lecture') and unpacks the claim in the same clause. Chunk 8-alt's 'The map at sitting 2' also resolves, not merely names: grep of curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/*.md shows 'sitting N' is an established convention for the Northwind four-sitting cut (plan-mode-done-right.md:86 uses 'the next sitting' the same way), and plan-mode-done-right.md — sitting 2 in that cut — is exactly the module that includes lectures/the-whole-map.md, so the callback is factually accurate for the variant where this chunk is live, not a where-does-the-deck-start guess.

This is a module file (metadata + LOs + ordered includes + framing per curriculum/CLAUDE.md's module-file shape); the guess/predict demo beats, if any, live inside the included lectures/exercises, out of this file's own scope.

Every chunk carries a self-standing claim or a named set of includes with framing prose: Big Idea's thesis sentence, Prework's artefact instruction, the five What-You'll-Learn LOs, Start here's framing plus blockquote, the worry-beside-the-artefact three-paragraph arc, Set-up-the-worktree's rationale plus four includes, the four Key Concepts lines, Bring-to-Module-6's carry-forward instruction, the two pre-read annotations, Next's two-sentence bridge. None is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

'Big Idea', 'Prework', 'What You'll Learn', 'Key Concepts', 'Next' are architecture-mandated canonical section names (curriculum/module-shape.md). 'Start here', 'Set up the worktree', 'Pre-reads before Module 6', 'Bring to Module 6', 'Back to the map, one last time' all match their chunk's content plainly. 'Hold the worry beside the artefact' is now a literal match — the body's own first instruction sentence is 'Hold that worry beside the artefact,' word-for-word off the header (this is the 2026-08-14 rewrite that replaced the prior header 'Your nag writes the verifier', which itself needed a maintainer-attested spirit-level read; the current pairing needs no such carve-out).

No 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction, no self-grading superlatives, no unlabeled-number-with-retraction, no abstraction-noun stacks, no empty-leg verb triplets in any chunk. Two- (not three-) item parallel constructions appear ('Ranked findings first, detail on request, the full record on disk' is actually three items but asyndetic listing, not repeated-opening-word anaphora/epistrophe; 'Where the return bears it out... Where it doesn't...' is a couplet; 'That control pays twice: a session your checks steer is a session you don't babysit, and a session you don't babysit can run beside another' is a two-leg list, each leg distinct; chunk 10's 'subtler misses, subtler drift' is a two-word couplet, not the banned three-leg anaphora/epistrophe pattern) — none trips the banned triple-construction rule, which requires three legs opening/closing on the same word with an empty third leg.

(Chunk 10 'Next' remains a clean two-sentence match for the same addendum — the corpus's own compliant specimen, unchanged.) This addendum is unnumbered in check_slides.md, so it is not counted toward the 14-rule completeness contract or toward blocking_findings_count/todos_count above.
